changes.before: Implement appendNote(notes,note). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Add one note at the end while keeping every earlier note.

before: Adding one record must preserve every earlier record and append the requested content. Checking only the new length could miss overwritten or incorrect records.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.

The array spread copies existing entries into a new array. The object spread copies the new record’s top-level fields. This is a shallow copy; nested objects would still need their own ownership policy.

Read the function call appendNote([{"id":1,"title":"Moon"}], {"id":2,"title":"Sea"}) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, appendNote runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
A result has the right length but replaces the old title. Has it met the append contract? The contract includes exact old content and the exact added item. Counts alone cannot establish either.
after: To append means to add at the end. A correct append keeps the old records in order and adds the supplied note after them. The result's length alone cannot prove that the content is right.
[...notes] starts a new array containing the existing items. The original array is not changed. Put the new note after those items.
{...note} creates a new object containing the added note's top-level fields. This keeps the added object separate from the original note object.

This is a shallow copy: it copies only the outer level. Existing note objects are shared with the old array, and any nested objects in the added note would still be shared. This function does not edit them.
Complete appendNote(notes, note). Return a new array with the existing records followed by a shallow copy of the supplied note. Leave both inputs unchanged.

project.title: Append without losing existing records
project.task: Complete appendNote(notes, note). Preserve the earlier records and append a shallow copy of the supplied note in a new array.
project.done_when: Both inputs stay unchanged, old records stay in order, and the requested note appears last.
